newsitem.title: JAPAN: Creditors sign Tobishima plan, debt cut to Y100 bln.
newsitem.headline: Creditors sign Tobishima plan, debt cut to Y100 bln.

text.p: Debt-ridden Tobishima Corp said in a statement on Monday that its creditors had formally agreed to a restructuring plan that reduces its group debt to 100 billion yen.
The construction firm reached a basic agreement with its creditors on the plan in March. It includes a reduction in creditors' claims against the builder to 100 billion yen from 740 billion yen.
Tobishima said it did not see any major changes in its parent earnings forecast for the year to March 31, 1998, which it announced in May.
In May, Tobishima said it expected parent current profits of five billion yen in 1997/98 on sales of 390 billion yen.
In 1996/97, the company posted an actual parent current profit of 10.07 billion yen on sales of 427.07 billion yen.
